children: delivered a largely positive Q3 2026 earnings performance, with Coca-Cola, Altria, and Colgate-Palmolive beating both EPS and revenue expectations, while Mondelez topped EPS estimates but narrowly missed revenue forecasts.

Eight companies from S&P 500 consumer staples sector reported earnings this week, with seven beating EPS estimates and one reporting in line with expectations. On the revenue front, seven companies topped consensus estimates, while one missed expectations.
Here’s a look at how the major companies performed:

adjusted EPS of $0.91, beating estimates by $0.03, while revenue increased 7.2% Y/Y to $13.4B, exceeding expectations by $470M. Strong international demand and 7% organic revenue growth supported results. Management raised its FY2026 comparable EPS growth outlook to at least 11%.

adjusted EPS of $1.52, up 4.8% Y/Y and $0.01 above estimates. Revenue rose 3.4% Y/Y to $5.44B, beating expectations by $130M. The company raised its FY2026 EPS guidance to $5.66–$5.74 and expanded its share repurchase program by $1B. Shares gained 5% following the results.

adjusted EPS of $0.78, beating estimates by $0.07, while revenue increased 2.4% Y/Y to $9.97B, missing expectations by $20M. Volume-led growth and improved margins supported earnings. Shares rose 3.5% after the announcement.

: Reported adjusted EPS of $0.97, beating estimates by $0.04, while revenue grew 4.7% Y/Y to $5.37B, exceeding expectations by $40M. Growth was supported by higher volumes and pricing gains. Management raised its FY2026 adjusted EPS growth outlook to 5%–7%.
